# 10 fixed prompts for the quality check. Score each answer 1–5. Do not edit after first use.
# --- reasoning (5)
1. A tank holds 1,200 litres. Pipe A fills it in 4 hours, pipe B empties it in 6 hours. Both open from empty: how long until full? Show steps.
2. Three boxes are labelled Apples, Oranges, Mixed. Every label is wrong. You may pick one fruit from one box. Which box, and how do you relabel all three?
3. A Postgres table has 50M rows and a query filtering on (customer_id, created_at) is slow. The only index is on created_at. What do you change and why, in order of expected impact?
4. Explain why LLM decoding on a CPU is limited by memory bandwidth rather than FLOPs, with a numeric example for a 7B model.
5. Two AWS accounts, same workload, one bill is 3x higher. List the first five things you check, most likely first.
# --- code (3)
6. Write a Python function that parses a CSV of (timestamp, bytes) and returns peak throughput in MB/s over any 60-second sliding window. Include a short test.
7. Write a bash script that finds the 10 largest files under a directory, excluding .git, and prints size and path, sorted descending.
8. Given this Terraform snippet with an S3 bucket, add server-side encryption, block public access, and a lifecycle rule moving objects to Glacier after 90 days. (Paste any minimal aws_s3_bucket resource.)
# --- writing (2)
9. Write a 120-word LinkedIn post announcing a benchmark of three CPU-only LLM engines. Direct tone, no hype, one concrete number placeholder.
10. Rewrite this sentence to be clearer and shorter: "Due to the fact that the system was not able to be accessed by the users at the time in question, a decision was made to roll back."
